partners.mechanism_chain: PLG (HGNC:9412) —DISRUPTS→ fibrinolysis (GO:0006574); fibrinolysis (GO:0006574) —LEADS_TO→ hypoplasminogenemia (MONDO:0009009); SERPINA1 (HGNC:10573) —DISRUPTS→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198); extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198) —LEADS_TO→ alpha 1-antitrypsin deficiency (MONDO:0013282); fibrinolysis (GO:0006574) —BINDS→ extracellular matrix organization (GO:0030198). Loss-of-function mutations in PLG impair fibrinolysis, leading to hypoplasminogenemia. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in SERPINA1 impair the inhibition of proteases like neutrophil elastase, which degrade extracellular matrix components. Both fibrinolysis and extracellular matrix organization are interconnected processes, and their dysregulation contributes to the distinct phenotypes of these diseases.

partners.mechanism_chain: PLG (HGNC:9109) —DISRUPTS→ Fibrinolysis (REACT:R-HSA-2020481); Fibrinolysis (REACT:R-HSA-2020481) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoplasminogenemia (MONDO:0009009); APOA1 (HGNC:610) —DISRUPTS→ Lipoprotein metabolism and clearance (REACT:R-HSA-389877); Lipoprotein metabolism and clearance (REACT:R-HSA-389877) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoalphalipoproteinemia, primary, 2, intermediate (MONDO:0859238); Lipoprotein metabolism and clearance (REACT:R-HSA-389877) —BINDS→ Fibrinolysis (REACT:R-HSA-2020481). Loss-of-function mutations in PLG disrupt fibrinolysis, leading to hypoplasminogenemia. Loss-of-function mutations in APOA1 disrupt lipoprotein metabolism. Both lipoprotein metabolism and fibrinolysis are interconnected pathways involved in lipid transport and vascular health. APOA1, as a component of HDL, plays a role in reverse cholesterol transport, and dysregulation can impact inflammatory processes and vascular integrity, indirectly affecting fibrinolytic function. Conversely, impaired fibrinolysis can lead to compromised clearance of fibrin and extracellular matrix components, potentially influencing lipid deposition and inflammatory responses within the vasculature.

partners.mechanism_chain: PLG (HGNC:9147) —PRODUCES→ Plasminogen (CHEBI:17709); Plasminogen (CHEBI:17709) —DISRUPTS→ Fibrinolysis (GO:0007596); Fibrinolysis (GO:0007596) —DECREASES→ Extracellular matrix remodeling (GO:0031012); Extracellular matrix remodeling (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ Hemorrhage (HP:0011421); APP variant (MONDO:0011583) —DISRUPTS→ Amyloid beta precursor protein (APP) (UniProt:P05060); Amyloid beta precursor protein (APP) (UniProt:P05060) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix remodeling (GO:0031012); Extracellular matrix remodeling (GO:0031012) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (HP:0002317). Gain-of-function mutations or altered processing of APP lead to its aggregation and deposition in cerebral blood vessels, also disrupting extracellular matrix remodeling and leading to cerebral amyloid angiopathy and associated hemorrhages. **Proposed mechanism:** PLG (HGNC:9167) —DISRUPTS→ Fibrinolysis (GO:0007596); Fibrinolysis (GO:0007596) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoplasminogenemia (MONDO:0009009); IGF2 (HGNC:5440) —DISRUPTS→ Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal Axis (GO:0007596); Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal Axis (GO:0007596) —LEADS_TO→ Silver-Russell syndrome 3 (MONDO:0014663). Loss-of-function mutations in PLG disrupt fibrinolysis, leading to hypoplasminogenemia. Variants in IGF2 can dysregulate the Hypothalamic-Pituitary-Adrenal (HPA) axis, contributing to Silver-Russell syndrome 3. The convergence is proposed at the level of the HPA axis, which can be influenced by growth factors like IGF2 and may have downstream effects that could indirectly impact systemic processes related to coagulation or inflammation, although a direct link to hypoplasminogenemia is speculative.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that genetic variants in IGF2 do not affect HPA axis activity or that PLG function is entirely independent of HPA axis regulation. _(variant: If a common variant (AF > 0.01) in the PLG gene is identified in gnomAD that fully rescues the hypoplasminogenemia phenotype, it would suggest alternative causal mechanisms or modifiers not captured by this hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding potential shared regulatory pathways, such as the HPA axis, could reveal novel therapeutic targets for diseases with disparate primary genetic causes but convergent downstream effects. For instance, modulating the HPA axis might offer a strategy to mitigate certain aspects of SRS3, and conversely, understanding systemic effects of hypoplasminogenemia could inform broader health management.

#### 9. amyloidosis, hereditary systemic 3  —  Tier 4 — Weak / Statistically Confounded  (fitness 0.200)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-114608, Reactome:R-HSA-381426)

**Proposed mechanism:** PLG (HGNC:9107) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoplasminogenemia (MONDO:0009009); APOA1 (HGNC:557) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal Apolipoprotein A-I (CHEBI:17086); Abnormal Apolipoprotein A-I (CHEBI:17086) —DISRUPTS→ Protein Misfolding and Aggregation (GO:0006460); PLG (HGNC:9107) —DISRUPTS→ Protein Misfolding and Aggregation (GO:0006460); Protein Misfolding and Aggregation (GO:0006460) —LEADS_TO→ Amyloidosis, hereditary systemic 3 (MONDO:0971008); Protein Misfolding and Aggregation (GO:0006460) —LEADS_TO→ Hypoplasminogenemia (MONDO:0009009). Loss-of-function mutations in PLG lead to hypoplasminogenemia, while loss-of-function mutations in APOA1 lead to the production of abnormal APOA1 that can misfold and aggregate. Both the deficiency of functional plasminogen and the aggregation of abnormal APOA1 contribute to a general pathway of protein misfolding and aggregation, which ultimately underlies the distinct phenotypes of these diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of any observed protein misfolding or aggregation in individuals with hypoplasminogenemia or carriers of APOA1 mutations would falsify this hypothesis. Specifically, if hypoplasminogenemia is found to be solely due to impaired fibrinolysis without any downstream effects on protein homeostasis or aggregation pathways, and amyloidosis 3 is solely due to APOA1 aggregation without any contribution from plasminogen-related pathways, the proposed overlap would be invalidated. _(variant: Identification of common benign variants (AF > 1%) in the PLG or APOA1 genes that are not associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway of protein misfolding and aggregation, even when initiated by distinct genetic defects (PLG vs. APOA1), could reveal common therapeutic targets. Strategies aimed at enhancing protein clearance, preventing protein aggregation, or stabilizing functional protein conformations might be applicable to both conditions, offering a potential avenue for novel therapeutic development.
